newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria invites Creditanstalt bids by Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: Austria invites Creditanstalt bids by Nov 15.

text.p: The Austrian government has invited new bids for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt-Bankverein by November 15, the finance ministry said in a statement on Monday.
Interested parties were asked to get in touch with investment house J.P. Morgan, the government's advisor in the long-delayed sale of the bank, for details of the bidding process.
No details of the offer for the government's 70 percent voting stake in the bank were made public. At current market prices, the stake would be worth around 14 billion schillings.
J.P. Morgan originally submitted a study of the bank a year ago, but Finance Minister Viktor Klima asked his advisors to update the report after he turned down the only known bidder last month.
Creditanstalt, the country's number-two bank, has topped the government's privatisation list for as long as six years.

A host of suitors has come and gone since the bank was put up for sale in 1990. The most recent bid by Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali was rejected by Klima since the group was reluctant to take on all of the government's 19.9 million ordinary shares in the bank.
